about: Board explorer data for boards.html, generated by tools/boards/chapter_data.py from boards.json and hotspots.json.

mcuBlock.name: RP2040 + CAN block
mcuBlock.summary: Every Talos board uses the same copy-pasted Altium device sheet: an RP2040, 16 MB flash, a 12 MHz crystal, a Tag-Connect SWD pad, reset/boot buttons, an RGB status LED, and an MCP2517FD SPI CAN FD controller with a TJA1442 transceiver and a slide switch for the 120 ohm termination (2 x 60.4 ohm, split).

parts.role: CAN termination on/off ("TERM ON" on the silk)

firmware_facts.text: The RP2040 makes a 4 MHz clock from its 48 MHz USB clock on GPIO21 and feeds it to the MCP2517FD, which multiplies it by 10 to 40 MHz. SPI runs at 20 MHz.
Pin map shared by every board: CAN controller on SPI0 (nCS 17, SCK 18, MOSI 19, MISO 20), clock out on 21, interrupt on 22, status LED on 13/14/15, debug UART TX on 16.
The termination switch state is read back through the controller (MCP2517FD_TERM_SENSE_ON_INT0).

mcuBlock.why: Mark 1 had I2C trouble over long wires (a 3 ft run to the depth sensor). Mark 2 put an RP2040 on every board and joined them with CAN instead of a shared I2C bus (story in the comments of tools/DeviceList.jsonc).

boards.name: POAC board
boards.statusBasis: confirmed: talos/PoacBoard firmware, DeviceList "Talos Poactuator Board", pretest_checks expects it at bus 1 id 1
boards.purpose: Takes both batteries, ORs them into one bus, makes the 15 V, 5 V, 12 V and 3.3 V rails, switches thruster power with the kill switch, measures the rails, and drives the torpedo/marker servo.
boards.why: Combines the Mark 2 power board and actuator board into one board to free space in the housing (team website). It keeps the power board's CAN ID 1, so software that looks for "the power board" still finds it.

firmwareFacts.text: Reads the physical kill switch on GPIO1 (interrupt on both edges) and drives SOFTWARE_KILL on GPIO2. GPIO2 starts in the kill state before safety is up.
Publishes state/kill every 150 ms and state/electrical every 1 s.

state/electrical: three_volt (ADC ch1, 10k/10k divider), balanced (ch2 = Vreg, 10k/1k), twelve_volt (ch3, which is wired to the 15 V rail), five_volt (ch4); port/stbd_powering from the LTC4412 STAT pins. port_voltage and stbd_voltage are sent as 0.
Turns the fan on at boot; command/electrical ENABLE_FANS / DISABLE_FANS switches it.

Drives one Hiwonder bus servo (half-duplex UART at 115200 baud from a PIO state machine on GPIO27) that indexes 2 torpedoes (240 and 200 deg) and 2 markers (0 and 50 deg). Firing is refused while killed or not armed.

revision.notes: Project PCB is PoactuatorPCB4 (ECO logs Jan 2024; PDF in the 2023-24 board-order release, Feb 2024). A Feb 2026 commit adds a separate 12 V output for the servo.

boards.name: ESC board
boards.statusBasis: confirmed: talos/ESCBoard firmware, CAN IDs 2 and 3, pretest_checks expects both
boards.purpose: Carries four APD 80F3 ESCs and talks to them with bidirectional DShot. Two identical boards drive the 8 thrusters.
boards.why: Bidirectional DShot gives RPM feedback on the same wire as the command. The APD firmware had no 3D (reversible) DShot mode, so the team patched the ESC firmware to add it.

firmwareFacts.text: DShot600, bidirectional, from PIO0; ESC UART telemetry read by PIO1.
Thrusters are held off for 5 s after ESC power appears (ESC_POWERUP_DELAY_MS 5000).
If no new RPM command arrives within 500 ms the thrusters stop, and stay off for 1 s.
ESC power counts as on above 9 V on VCC_MEAS.
Core 1 runs the RPM controller; disabled_flags explain why it is off: SAFETY_KILLED, ESC_BOARD_OFF, ESC_POWERON_DELAY, TGT_RPM_STALE, TGT_RPM_STALE_PENALTY, CONTROLLER_UNCONFIGURED.
The board reads the ID jumper on GPIO29 at boot: 0 -> CAN client 2, 1 -> CAN client 3.
Uses 7 pole pairs to turn electrical RPM into shaft RPM.

revision.notes: Designed for Tempest Mark 2 (Jan 2023) and reused on Talos. The repo has later edits (Oct-Dec 2025: a voltage protector, traces); unconfirmed whether the boards in Talos were rebuilt.

boards.name: Camera cage breakout board
boards.statusBasis: confirmed: talos/CameraCageBB firmware, CAN ID 4, pretest_checks expects it
boards.purpose: Power and I/O hub of the camera cage: switches Orin power, reads the depth sensor, runs fans and the RGB status strip, injects power into the DVL Ethernet cable, and joins the Orin to both CAN buses.

firmwareFacts.text: Reads the depth sensor as an MS5837-02BA on I2C (200 kHz) and publishes state/depth/raw in frame talos/pressure_link.
Turns the Orin switch and the fans on at boot.
Drives the RGB status strip from PIO0; command/led messages with the CCB target bit set it.
Still creates a state/leak publisher, but its periodic publish is commented out. The team no longer uses the leak sensor.

revision.notes: Mark 2 design (Jan 2023). Last commit 2024-11-10 "Added connectors and LDOs".

boards.name: IVC board
boards.statusBasis: confirmed: talos/IVCBoard firmware, CAN ID 8, DeviceList "Talos IVC Board", pretest_checks expects it
boards.purpose: Acoustic modem for talking to the second vehicle: drives a transducer and listens on a hydrophone. Also has a Bluetooth audio module that can play sound through the transducer.

firmwareFacts.text: Two-tone FSK: 17 kHz and 19 kHz, 50 ms per symbol; packets are 8 data bits + a 4-bit CRC.
Receive uses an FFT (kiss FFT) on the ADC samples.
Schematic note: "Populate SB5 0 ohm for Lil' Boat, DNP for Talos". The firmware picks its Talos thresholds when GPIO6 (BOARD_ID_PIN) reads low.

revision.notes: Designed Mar-Apr 2025 ("ivc board ready to go out confirmed" 2025-03-19, "fixed opa548 lead mix-up" 2025-04-06).
